Just a quick update - i will do a longer one for March on Substack (my intention is certainly not to only post green!) but between getting daycare flu, maintaining ALPHAPORT and general investing over the Iran situation, keeping all the plates spinning has been rough the last couple weeks.

In any case we entered the weekend in good shape, surely outperforming SPY at this point, though the relative weakness in software has significantly dragged on returns (even @bstaples has not been able to save $GTLB yet but i continue my prayers to the DevSecOps spirits). I think it will work out, but i would be lying if i told you i hadn't simply anchored the new price to a new story (eg the company is surely worth a 30% premium in an acquisition here and thus, if it gets bought out in 2 years, a fairly negative scenario still yields a 15% a year return).

Shorts have also significantly dragged returns (should i have closed out the Quantum shorts when they levelled off rather than deferring taxes and using them for funding? maybe something to consider later), but it is kind of two sides of the same coin in this massive run up, saying that shitcoin memestocks like $LWLG should be down but $SNDK should still be up bigly because it actually has earnings is just kind of disingenous - probably the reality is $LWLG should be down and $SNDK should be up but a little less until things get proven out - i am in the $1500 price target camp on this one, but also 50% in a month is a bit much, the market has gotten a little too forward looking.

On the winners side, $DAVE continues to be the gift that keeps on giving - i started my position in this company at $4 a share, but have averaged up many times over the last 2 years. I have kept a few of the initial lots, to see if we can hit the fabled 100 bagger on this one, but also have bought much higher, at 90, and then again at 170 etc. This one is a good reminder that often you should just buy more of the thing you understand well that is working rather than dabbling with supply chain bottlenecks at 30x sales.

In terms of new ideas I am increasingly interested in, I think the EDA space is where i will concentrate more of my attention next week. I bought starter positions in $SNPS and $CDNS. I've owned $SNPS before, but its kind of interesting here. It's going to be a slow grower for a bit. But more importantly, I am increasingly interested in what happens with this concept of headless software (eg Agents using the software without a UI). Jensen discussed this on the latest Dwarkesh podcast, but it does make a tonne of sense - once this simulation software gets very good and integrates physics perfectly ($SNPS uses Ansys's tools for this, and they are integrated with Omniverse) you will simply run unlimited 'jobs' with the design agents and do simulated testing. It's possible this simulated testing dramatically reduces the need for physical testing - a huge industry in semiconductors. After all, why not - in Aerospace, you are doing all the simulations on the computer, then you actually have to build the rocket or plane to test it - cost of failure at that point is high! And yet, it all works. There's no reason to think we can't get increasingly large amounts of the testing done at the simulation level.

The implied end state however is pretty bullish these EDA companies - that you are designing and testing semiconductors with massive headless agent swarms-  rather than doing just 2-3 designs you are doing 1000 to test every possible permutation that could work, etc. This kind of workflow could apply to most advanced manufacturing. In fact, if you use coding as an analog, the end state is that you will have 1 design engineer monitoring agents that do 100x as much work as before. This will take a while to get right, EDA is way more complicated than shipping a database, but it seems like it is very doable especially with modest model improvements from here.

Anyway, without getting too long, it's an interesting thing to consider.

Enjoy your weekend!

Martin

shorted $AXTI. only 1% but my basic thesis is here: https://t.co/bItTJiRCgq
Serenity can spin a good yarn, but the reality is Sumitomo Electric has equivalent or better capability at manufacturing InP and can bring more supply online fairly quickly if margins explode. There are also other players in the game.
People point to the actual indium resource as a potential supply bottle neck (and suggest AXTI has ownership of the actual resources as well as the InP production capacity), but the amount of indium necessary for a huge photonics buildout is minimal.

Management knows its heavily overvalued, hence the at the market offering to raise 500m. You can say 'reflexivity' eg ponzinomics = how you win, but $AXTI is not OpenAI. You need to be able to create a really good business at the end of the ponzi at this valuation - creating artificial superintelligence is barely good enough, growing InP wafers aint it.

I thought about pairing it with LONG Sumitomo Electric $5802 but too much of their rev is from automotive components (historically a terrible business) to get excited about PE 30. That said, i think S.E. is well run, operating cash flow is high and we do have major earnings growth, so in the world of physical AI i think SE will still do well. Just think there's probably better spots.

Price action on a lot of these names is nutty, look at how much u have to pay for puts on $AXTI rather than shorting common? People are super afraid of pumps, liquidity etc. $36.47 break even in January for a $85 stock. Max upside is what, a 2x if it goes to 0? (Not happening)

@citrini called this perfectly nice one.
But the reason it’s a popular funding short is because if u paired it with LONG literally anything else (memory, CPU, optics, etc) you are up even when it went completely against you. I remain short tho, $QCOM just has a terrible market position in all its markets (compete w NVDA on cars, INTC/AMD on DC CPUs, Samsung and Google on their own phones etc).

China is a material amount of revenue. On top of this Apple is aggressively working to cutout their modem and increasingly shipping models without it. But the main models still use it, so long term this presents another revenue headwind. All of this would be fine if the company was cheap, but it’s really not that cheap?

Still a very nice call though, basically got everything right which means he could have bought a bunch of calls going into earnings with a very tight expiration date and got a much better result than just being long.

referenced.text:
My hottest and most wrong (year to date) take is also probably the only semi stock that Zephyr and I currently disagree on. Since December I’ve been bullish QCOM and he’s been bearish. Of course, he has been hugely right and I have not been - but I really think that’s going to change over the next 12 months.

I also like owning it because it’s a pretty popular funding short that sims a potential beneficiary of any breakthrough in edge (or breakthrough in memory efficiency like if someone can get PIM to work). So you could imagine a scenario where any significant progress for on-device inference leads to moderating expectations* for data center growth, the popular longs take a hit and QCOM squeezes hard both on improving outlook and a squeeze.

It’s also just cheap af and eventually the circumstances causing its underperformance will abate and people will still buy phones and eventually it’ll have its day. In the meantime, I see it kind of like a positive expected value hedge against a shock to estimates that could end up being too optimistic if just, like, 20% of inference is done on device.

(*I really do mean moderating, I don’t think edge AI / on-device inference means we don’t use data centers anymore obviously. We’re not going to use the AI on our mobile phones to design drugs or run complex systems obviously, but I could see some revisions when some of the demand of “hey ChatGPT, <insert thing you could otherwise google>” isn’t running through the cloud)
